desc.es: Hablar de hábitos y tendencias, presentes y pasados

grammarIntro.es:
Hablar de tendencias

tend to + verboI tend to get up late at weekends. (suelo)
will (hábito típico, característico)She'll spend hours reading if you let her.
would (hábito pasado)As a child I would hide under the table.
keep (on) + -ingHe keeps forgetting his keys. (no para de)

Hábitos que molestan: always + continuo

Con always / constantly / forever el presente o el pasado continuo expresa irritación:

You're always leaving your socks on the floor! (¡siempre dejas…!)
She was constantly complaining about her job.
Compara: He always arrives on time (dato neutro) / He's always arriving late! (queja). El acento va en always.
«Suelo» en presente nunca es use to: ✗ I use to go → ✓ I usually go / I tend to go. Would no sirve para estados del pasado: ✗ I would have a dog → ✓ I used to have a dog.

desc.es: Tiempos narrativos: el pasado perfecto continuo y los conectores de una historia

grammarIntro.es:
Pasado perfecto continuo

had been + -ing. Actividad que duraba hasta un momento del pasado (o justo antes). Pone el foco en la duración o en la causa de algo visible:

The ground was wet. It had been raining all night.
She was exhausted because she had been working for twelve hours.
We had been walking for an hour when we realised we were lost.
Past perfect simplePast perfect continuous
acción terminada, resultado, cantidadactividad, duración
She had written three chapters.She had been writing since dawn.

Conectores narrativos

As soon as he arrived, …en cuanto llegó
By the time we got there, the shop had closed.para cuando llegamos
Eventually, they found the way.al final (tras mucho tiempo)
Meanwhile, …mientras tanto
No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.nada más sentarme (formal, con inversión)
Los verbos de estado no van en continuo: ✗ I had been knowing her → ✓ I had known her for years.

grammarIntro.es:
Futuro continuo

will be + -ing: algo que estará en curso en un momento futuro; también planes que siguen su curso normal:

This time tomorrow I'll be lying on a beach. (estaré tumbado)
Will you be using the car tonight? (pregunta educada por los planes)

Futuro perfecto

will have + participio: algo que ya habrá terminado antes de un momento futuro, normalmente con by:

By 2030, they will have finished the new airport.
By the time you arrive, I'll have cooked dinner.

Otras expresiones de futuro

be about to + verboThe film is about to start. (está a punto de)
be on the point of + -ingI was on the point of leaving when she called.
be due to + verboThe train is due to arrive at 6. (está previsto)
be bound to + verboIt's bound to rain. (seguro que…)
be likely / unlikely toPrices are likely to rise.
Tras by the time, when, as soon as, until, presente aunque hable del futuro: ✗ by the time you will arrive → ✓ by the time you arrive.

desc.es: Modales en pasado: deducciones, críticas y arrepentimientos

grammarIntro.es:
Deducir sobre el pasado

casi seguro que símust have + participioThe streets are wet. It must have rained.
posiblemight / may / could haveShe might have missed the bus.
casi seguro que nocan't / couldn't haveHe can't have seen us. He didn't say hello.

Criticar y lamentar

should have / ought to havelo correcto habría sido (no se hizo)You should have told me!
shouldn't havese hizo, y fue un errorI shouldn't have eaten so much.
could haveposibilidad no aprovechada; reprocheYou could have hurt yourself! You could have called.

needn't have / didn't need to

I needn't have brought an umbrella. (lo traje y no hacía falta)
I didn't need to bring an umbrella. (no hacía falta; normalmente no lo traje)
En la conversación suenan reducidos: should've, must've, could've /ʃʊdəv/. Por eso los nativos a veces escriben mal «should of». ✗ must had → ✓ must have + participio. Fíjate: «debió de llover» = it must have rained; «debería haber llamado» = I should have called.

title.es: Si las cosas hubieran sido distintas

desc.es: Condicionales mixtos y alternativas a if

grammarIntro.es:
Condicionales mixtos

Combinan tiempos distintos en la condición y en el resultado:

Condición pasada → resultado presenteCondición presente → resultado pasado
If I had taken that job, I'd be rich now.If I weren't so shy, I'd have spoken to her.
(if + past perfect, would + verbo)(if + past simple, would have + participio)

Alternativas a if

unlessa menos queI won't go unless you come.
provided / providing (that), as long assiempre queYou can borrow it as long as you're careful.
suppose / supposing¿y si…?, supongamos queSuppose you lost your job, what would you do?
even ifaunque (incluso si)I'll go even if it rains.
otherwisesi no, de lo contrarioHurry, otherwise we'll be late.

Condicionales con inversión (formal)

Should you need help, call me. (= If you should need…)
Had I known, I would have come. (= If I had known…)
Were I in your position, I'd resign. (= If I were…)
✗ Unless you don't hurry → ✓ Unless you hurry (unless ya es negativo). even if ≠ even though: even though = aunque (es un hecho).

inverted conditionals (Should you…, Had I known…)

desc.es: El pasado irreal: wish, if only, I'd rather, it's time

grammarIntro.es:
wish + would

Para quejarse de lo que otra persona hace (o no hace) y nos gustaría que cambiara:

I wish you would stop interrupting me. (ojalá dejaras de…)
I wish it would stop raining.
wish + pasadosituación presente irrealI wish I lived nearer.
wish + past perfectarrepentimiento pasadoI wish I hadn't gone.
wish + wouldqueja, deseo de cambio de otroI wish he would listen.
No se usa wish + would con uno mismo: ✗ I wish I would… → ✓ I wish I could… Para deseos posibles de futuro se usa hope: I hope you pass (✗ I wish you pass).

I'd rather · It's time · as if

I'd rather + forma base (yo)I'd rather stay in.
I'd rather + otra persona + pasadoI'd rather you didn't smoke here. (preferiría que no fumaras)
It's (high) time + sujeto + pasadoIt's time we went home. It's high time you found a job.
as if / as though + pasado (irreal)He talks as if he knew everything.
Todas estas estructuras usan el pasado con valor irreal, igual que el español usa el imperfecto de subjuntivo: «preferiría que no fumaras», «ya es hora de que nos fuéramos».

desc.es: La pasiva avanzada: impersonal, con dos objetos y causativa

grammarIntro.es:
Pasiva impersonal

Típica de las noticias, para opiniones y rumores sin decir quién los dice:

It + pasiva + thatSujeto + pasiva + to-infinitivo
It is said that he is very rich.He is said to be very rich.
It is believed that the thief escaped.The thief is believed to have escaped.
It is expected that prices will rise.Prices are expected to rise.
Si lo dicho es anterior al momento en que se dice, usa el infinitivo perfecto: She is thought to have left the country (se cree que se ha ido). Verbos típicos: say, believe, think, know, report, expect, consider, estimate, allege.

Pasiva con dos objetos

They gave her a prize. → She was given a prize. (lo más natural en inglés)
They sent me the documents. → I was sent the documents.

Causativa y be supposed to

have / get + objeto + participioI'm having my car repaired. She got her bag stolen. (le robaron)
be supposed toYou're supposed to wear a helmet. (se supone que; deberías) · The film is supposed to be good. (dicen que)
El español dice «se dice / se cree»; el inglés no usa reflexivo: ✗ It says that he is rich (= el texto dice) → ✓ It is said that he is rich.

gnames: impersonal passive: It is said that… / He is said to…

desc.es: Verbos para contar lo que otros dicen y sus estructuras

grammarIntro.es:
Patrones de los verbos de habla

PatrónVerbosEjemplo
+ to + verboagree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, claimHe refused to help.
+ objeto + toadvise, persuade, encourage, remind, urge, warn, invite, tell, askShe persuaded me to stay.
+ -ingadmit, deny, suggest, recommend, regretHe denied stealing the money.
+ preposición + -ingapologise for, insist on, accuse sb of, blame sb for, congratulate sb on, thank sb forThey accused him of lying.
+ that + fraseexplain, complain, announce, admit, deny, suggest, insist, promiseShe explained that the shop was closed.
suggest nunca lleva objeto + to: ✗ He suggested me to go → ✓ He suggested going / He suggested that I (should) go. Igual con recommend.
Estos verbos resumen mejor que say la intención de lo dicho. «"Fui yo", dijo» → He admitted doing it. «"Te lo devuelvo mañana"» → She promised to give it back.

grammarIntro.es:
Preposición + relativo

Informal (preposición al final)Formal (preposición delante)
the man (who) I spoke tothe man to whom I spoke
the house (that) I grew up inthe house in which I grew up
Tras preposición: whom (personas) y which (cosas), nunca who ni that: ✗ the man to who / ✗ the house in that.

Cuantificador + of whom / of which

I have three brothers, all of whom live abroad. (todos los cuales)
She bought ten books, most of which were second-hand.
The flats, none of which have a lift, are cheap.

what y oraciones reducidas

what = lo queWhat I need is a holiday.
relativa reducida con -ing (activa)People living in the centre (= who live) pay more.
relativa reducida con participio (pasiva)Houses built before 1900 (= which were built) …
whereby (formal) = por el cual, mediante el cual: a system whereby residents can vote online.

desc.es: Oraciones de participio para escribir con más fluidez

grammarIntro.es:
¿Qué son?

Frases sin sujeto ni verbo conjugado que sustituyen a una oración con when, because, after, if… Son típicas de la lengua escrita:

Oración completaOración de participio
When she opened the door, she saw…Opening the door, she saw…
Because I didn't know what to do, I called…Not knowing what to do, I called…
After he had finished, he left.Having finished, he left.
The book, which was written in 1900, …Written in 1900, the book…

Tres formas

-ing (activo, simultáneo o causa)Feeling tired, I went to bed.
having + participio (anterior)Having lived in Japan, she speaks Japanese.
participio (pasivo)Built in 1890, the bridge is still in use.
El sujeto implícito tiene que ser el mismo que el de la oración principal. ✗ Walking down the street, a car hit me (¡el coche iba andando!) → ✓ Walking down the street, I was hit by a car.
Con preposiciones también: On arriving, she called her mother (nada más llegar). After finishing university, he travelled.

desc.es: Estructuras enfáticas: oraciones escindidas, do enfático y otros recursos

grammarIntro.es:
Oraciones escindidas (cleft sentences)

Dividen la frase para destacar una parte, como el español «Lo que…es…» / «Fue… quien…»:

NeutraEnfática
I need a holiday.What I need is a holiday.
His attitude annoys me.What annoys me is his attitude.
Tom broke the window.It was Tom who broke the window.
I met her in Paris.It was in Paris that I met her.
I only want to sleep.All I want is to sleep.
We left because of the noise.The reason (why) we left was the noise.

do / does / did enfáticos

En afirmativas, el auxiliar añade énfasis o contraste («sí que…»):

I do like your dress! (¡sí que me gusta!)
She says I never help, but I did help yesterday!
Do sit down. (invitación insistente, educada)
Con What… is + verbo: What I did was (to) call the police. Otros recursos: the thing is…, the problem is…, the point is…, the place where….
✗ That I need is a rest → ✓ What I need is a rest. ✗ It was Tom which broke it → ✓ It was Tom who broke it.

the thing / the reason / the place… is

desc.es: Patrones verbales avanzados: objeto + infinitivo, make / let, infinitivos y gerundios perfectos y pasivos

grammarIntro.es:
Verbo + objeto + to

Donde el español usa «que + subjuntivo», el inglés usa objeto + to-infinitivo:

I want you to come. (quiero que vengas — ✗ I want that you come)
They expect us to work late. · I'd like him to call me.

make y let

make sb + forma baseobligarShe made me apologise.
let sb + forma basedejar, permitirMy parents let me stay out late.
pasiva: be made to(con to)I was made to apologise.

Formas perfectas y pasivas

to have + participioI'm glad to have met you. He seems to have left.
having + participioShe denied having taken it.
to be + participioI want to be told the truth.
being + participioI hate being interrupted.

Expresiones fijas con -ing

It's no use crying. · It's not worth waiting. · There's no point (in) arguing. · I can't help laughing. · I object to paying more. · She's committed to helping others.
En object to, look forward to, be used to, be committed to, admit to, to es preposición → -ing: ✗ I look forward to hear → ✓ to hearing.

desc.es: Phrasal verbs de tres palabras y del mundo laboral

grammarIntro.es:
Phrasal verbs de tres palabras

Verbo + partícula + preposición. Son inseparables: el objeto siempre va al final.

come up withidear, proponerShe came up with a great idea.
put up withaguantarI can't put up with this noise.
catch up with / keep up withalcanzar / seguir el ritmoI can't keep up with the news.
cut down onreducir (consumo)I'm cutting down on sugar.
get away withsalir impuneHe got away with it.
look up to / look down onadmirar / despreciarShe looks up to her grandmother.

En el trabajo

take oncontratar; asumirlay offdespedir (por falta de trabajo)
take overhacerse cargo; absorbercarry outllevar a cabo
step downdimitir, dejar el cargofall throughfracasar, venirse abajo (un plan)
follow uphacer seguimientofill in forsustituir a alguien
point outseñalarsort outsolucionar
Las partículas tienen significados frecuentes: up = completamente (eat up, use up); out = hasta el final, a fondo (work out, sort out); down = reducir (cut down, slow down); on = continuar (carry on, go on).

desc.es: Prefijos y sufijos para ampliar el vocabulario

grammarIntro.es:
Prefijos negativos

un-unhappy, unreliable, unlikely
in- / im- / ir- / il-inaccurate, impossible (ante p, m, b), irresponsible (ante r), illegal (ante l)
dis-dishonest, disagree, disappear
mis- (mal)misunderstand, misspell, mislead

Otros prefijos

over- (demasiado)overcooked, overestimate, oversleepunder- (demasiado poco)underpaid, underestimate
re- (otra vez)rewrite, reconsider, rebuildpre- / post-prehistoric, postgraduate
co- (juntos)co-worker, cooperateex-ex-wife, ex-president

Sufijos

SustantivosAdjetivosVerbos
-ness (happiness), -ment (improvement), -ity (ability), -tion/-sion (explanation), -ance/-ence (appearance, existence), -ship (friendship), -hood (childhood)-ful (useful), -less (careless), -ous (dangerous), -ive (effective), -able/-ible (reliable, flexible), -al (natural), -ic (scientific)-ise/-ize (modernise), -en (widen, shorten), -ify (simplify)
En el examen de la EOI es típica la tarea de «word formation»: mira qué categoría necesita el hueco (sustantivo tras artículo, adjetivo antes de sustantivo, adverbio junto al verbo) y si el sentido es negativo. -ful y -less son opuestos: careful / careless, useful / useless.
✗ unpossible, ✗ inlegal → ✓ impossible, ✓ illegal. ✗ disreliable → ✓ unreliable. Cuidado con los cambios: explain → explanation, pronounce → pronunciation, strong → strength.

desc.es: Preguntas avanzadas: question tags especiales, preguntas negativas y respuestas cortas

grammarIntro.es:
Question tags: casos especiales

I'm late, aren't I?(no amn't I)
Let's go, shall we?propuesta
Open the window, will you / could you?imperativo
Nobody called, did they?nobody / nothing ya son negativos → tag afirmativo
Everyone was there, weren't they?everyone/somebody → they
There's a problem, isn't there?there is → there
La entonación cambia el sentido: bajando = esperas que te den la razón; subiendo = pregunta real, no estás seguro.

Preguntas negativas

Didn't you hear the alarm? (sorpresa: ¿no oíste…?)
Wouldn't it be better to wait? (sugerencia)
Isn't it beautiful! (exclamación)
Al responder a una pregunta negativa, yes / no se refieren a la realidad, no a la pregunta: — Didn't you go? — No (= no fui) / Yes, I did (= sí fui). El español funciona al revés a menudo, ¡cuidado!

Respuestas cortas y acuerdo

— I love jazz. — So do I.— I can't swim. — Neither / Nor can I.
— Will it rain? — I hope not. / I'm afraid so.— Is she coming? — I think so. / I don't think so.
